questions.q: What is the rhyme scheme of a Shakespearean sonnet, and how many lines does it contain?
questions.a: A Shakespearean sonnet has 14 lines with the rhyme scheme abab cdcd efef gg. A wrong answer (e.g., "abba abba cde cde" or "12 lines") reveals confusion with the Petrarchan sonnet form or a lack of recall of the basic structural definition.

questions.q: In the poem, the first quatrain defines love by saying what it is *not*. Why does the poet choose this negative definition strategy instead of a positive one?
questions.a: The negative definition ("Love is not love which alters...") establishes the absolute constancy of true love by excluding all changeability; it forces the reader to conceive of love as an unchanging essence rather than a list of variable attributes. A wrong answer (e.g., "to make the poem sound sad") shows the student misses the logical function of negation in building an argument.

questions.q: Identify the volta in this sonnet. At which line does it occur, and what shift in the argument does it mark?
questions.a: The volta occurs at line 9 ("O no, it is an ever-fixed mark"), shifting from defining love by negation (what it is not) to a positive affirmation using extended metaphors (the fixed mark, the star). A wrong answer (e.g., placing the volta at the couplet) indicates the student does not recognize that the turn in a Shakespearean sonnet often begins the third quatrain, not the couplet.

questions.q: Compare the metaphor of the "ever-fixed mark" (line 5) with the metaphor of the "star" (line 7). How do they work together to develop the poem's central argument in the second quatrain?
questions.a: The "ever-fixed mark" (a sea-mark/beacon) suggests stability amid storms, while the "star" (Polaris) suggests guidance for lost ships ("wandering bark"); together they portray love as both an unshakeable anchor and an active guide, deepening the definition from mere endurance to purposeful direction. A wrong answer that treats them as separate, unrelated images shows failure to synthesize the metaphorical cluster.

questions.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of the final couplet ("If this be error...") as a conclusion. Does it strengthen or undermine the poem's authority? Justify your view.
questions.a: The couplet strengthens the poem's authority by staking the poet's entire reputation on the truth of the argument: if the definition is wrong, then no poetry exists and no one has ever loved — an impossible condition that rhetorically proves the definition's certainty. A wrong answer calling it "arrogant" or "weak" misses the rhetorical device of *reductio ad absurdum* that closes the logical structure.

questions.q: Write a four-line stanza (quatrain) in iambic pentameter that continues the poem's argument by describing what true love does *not* do in the face of human mortality, using the same negative definition strategy as the first quatrain.
questions.a: A strong response will maintain iambic pentameter (da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM), use an abab rhyme scheme, and employ negative statements (e.g., "Love does not fade when breath departs the frame, / Nor counts the dust that covers beauty's name..."). A poor answer ignores meter, rhyme, or the negative strategy, revealing gaps in both structural awareness and poetic technique.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: In a ______ sonnet, "plot and narrative structure" refers to the logical progression of the poem's argument through its fixed formal divisions: three quatrains (four-line stanzas) that develop a central idea, a volta (turn) that shifts the perspective, and a concluding couplet that resolves or summarizes the argument.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you open the poem and see a block of 14 lines — you might wonder where to even ______.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you open the poem and see a block of ______ lines — you might wonder where to even begin.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can independently divide the sonnet into its structural units (quatrains and couplet), identify the rhyme scheme, locate the volta, trace the argument across the quatrains, and explain how the structure reinforces the theme of constancy.
